Both aws and onprem profiles deploy without config errors | REQ-002, REQ-011 | Infra | open | ### Functional Scope — REQ-001 This REQ establishes the canonical data contract backbone for the entire Zen 2030 platform. It is the foundational REQ that all application, AI, and infra REQs depend on for consistent entity naming, lifecycle state definitions, audit fields, and persistence rules. This REQ belongs to the broader scenario of building a GDPR-compliant, auditable document management platform where documents pass through a strict lifecycle: Pending → Processing → AwaitingValidation → Validated → Archived → Exported. Human validation is mandatory before Validated state is reachable. **Delivered now:** - SQLAlchemy ORM models for: Document, DocumentVersion, IngestRecord, ValidationRecord, WorkflowTask, AuditLog, ExportRecord, User, Role, RoleAssignment - Alembic migration baseline with all tables, indexes, and constraints - pgvector extension enablement migration for the ai_embeddings column on Document - Lifecycle state enum: Pending, Processing, AwaitingValidation, Validated, Archived, Exported, Rejected - Audit fields on all mutable entities: created_at, updated_at, created_by, updated_by, deleted_at (soft delete) - Business key definitions: document_id (UUID), ingest_ref, classification_category, confidence_score - Core relationship definitions: Document → DocumentVersion (1:N), Document → ValidationRecord (1:N), Document → AuditLog (1:N) - Seed migration for default roles: admin, validator, operator, viewer **Intentionally deferred:** - Application-layer business logic (belongs to REQ-003 through REQ-012) - Profile-specific storage adapters (REQ-002) - Auth integration (REQ-011) - Vector embedding population (REQ-012) **Future REQs may safely assume:** - All entity names, field names, state enum values, and relationship cardinalities defined here are stable - Alembic is the only migration tool; no raw DDL outside migrations - pgvector is available on the target Postgres 16 instance - Soft delete pattern is canonical; hard deletes are forbidden on Document and AuditLog ### Technical Scope — REQ-001 - **Lane:** sql + python (SQLAlchemy models + Alembic migrations) - **Runtime profile:** aws and on-prem (same schema, same migrations, profile-independent) - **Primary module:** `data.models` (ORM entity definitions), `data.migrations` (Alembic env and versions) - **Main module boundary:** `src/data/` — models, base, enums, migrations - **Database:** PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector extension - **ORM:** SQLAlchemy 2.x (async-compatible declarative base) - **Migration tool:** Alembic with autogenerate disabled; all migrations hand-authored for auditability - **Key entities:** Document, DocumentVersion, IngestRecord, ValidationRecord, WorkflowTask, AuditLog, ExportRecord, User, Role, RoleAssignment - **State enum:** DocumentState (Pending, Processing, AwaitingValidation, Validated, Archived, Exported, Rejected) — defined as Python Enum and Postgres native enum type - **Audit fields:** created_at (timestamptz), updated_at (timestamptz), created_by (UUID FK to User), updated_by (UUID FK to User), deleted_at (nullable timestamptz) - **pgvector:** `embedding vector(1024)` column on Document for bge-m3 embeddings; index type ivfflat deferred to REQ-012 - **Indexes:** document_id (PK UUID), state (btree), classification_category (btree), created_at (btree), ingest_ref (unique) - **Test expectations:** Alembic upgrade/downgrade round-trip test; model instantiation tests; state enum coverage; relationship integrity tests - **Documentation:** inline docstrings on all models; ERD diagram in `docs/data/ERD.md` - **Gate:** migrations must apply cleanly on a fresh Postgres 16 container; no data loss on downgrade of baseline - **Forbidden:** raw DDL outside Alembic, hard deletes on Document or AuditLog, model duplication in application layers - **New modules allowed:** Yes — `src/data/` is new ### Acceptance — REQ-001 - `alembic upgrade head` completes without error on a fresh Postgres 16 container with pgvector extension installed - `alembic downgrade base` followed by `alembic upgrade head` produces identical schema (round-trip clean) - All ORM models instantiate without error and all required fields are present and typed correctly - DocumentState enum contains exactly: Pending, Processing, AwaitingValidation, Validated, Archived, Exported, Rejected - AuditLog and Document entities have created_at, updated_at, created_by, updated_by, deleted_at fields with correct nullability - pgvector `embedding vector(1024)` column exists on Document and the pgvector extension is confirmed active - Default roles (admin, validator, operator, viewer) are present in the seed migration - Unit tests cover model instantiation, relationship traversal, and state enum values with ≥80% coverage on `src/data/` - ERD diagram is present at `docs/data/ERD.md` and reflects all entities ### Out of Scope — REQ-001 - Application business logic, API endpoints, or service classes - Profile-specific adapter wiring (REQ-002) - Auth token validation or RBAC enforcement (REQ-011) - Vector embedding population or RAG index creation (REQ-012) - Multi-tenant schema partitioning ### Future Compatibility — REQ-001 - All downstream REQs (REQ-003 through REQ-013) must import ORM models exclusively from `src/data/models` - State enum values must not be renamed or removed; new states may be added only via new Alembic migration - Audit field names (created_at, updated_at, created_by, updated_by, deleted_at) are stable contracts - pgvector column name `embedding` on Document is stable for REQ-012 - Role names (admin, validator, operator, viewer) are stable for REQ-011 RBAC wiring --- ### Functional Scope — REQ-002 This REQ establishes the profile adapter layer that isolates all infrastructure differences between the `aws` and `onprem` deployment profiles behind stable interface contracts. It is a mandatory prerequisite for all application REQs that touch object storage, queuing, eventing, or secrets. This REQ belongs to the broader scenario of delivering functional parity across AWS and on-prem deployments. The architecture principle is: business APIs and lifecycle semantics remain profile-independent; infrastructure differences are isolated behind adapter contracts. **Delivered now:** - Abstract interface definitions for: ObjectStorageAdapter, QueueAdapter, EventAdapter, SecretsAdapter - AWS implementations: S3Adapter (boto3), SQSAdapter, SNSAdapter, SecretsManagerAdapter - On-prem implementations: S3CompatibleAdapter (boto3 with endpoint override), ApprovedQueueAdapter (configurable broker), ApprovedEventAdapter, VaultAdapter (or approved on-prem secret store) - Profile resolver: reads `DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE` env var (`aws` or `onprem`) and returns the correct adapter instance via factory - Configuration schema: profile-specific env vars documented and validated at startup via Pydantic Settings - Local development mode: MinIO for object storage, Redis Streams or lightweight queue for messaging, env-file-based secrets - Adapter health-check endpoints callable from observability layer **Intentionally deferred:** - Observability sink adapters (REQ-014) - AI runtime adapters (REQ-012) - Full secrets rotation logic (operational concern) **Future REQs may safely assume:** - All application code accesses object storage, queues, events, and secrets exclusively via adapter interfaces from `infra.adapters` - Profile resolution is deterministic at startup; no runtime profile switching - Local dev mode is always available for all adapter types ### Technical Scope — REQ-002 - **Lane:** python (backend) - **Runtime profile:** aws, on-prem, local (all three must be concretely implemented) - **Primary module:** `src/infra/adapters/` — storage, queue, event, secrets sub-packages - **Interface pattern:** Python abstract base classes (ABC) with typed method signatures - **AWS implementations:** boto3 for S3, SQS, SNS; boto3 for Secrets Manager - **On-prem implementations:** boto3 with `endpoint_url` override for S3-compatible storage; configurable queue client; Vault HVAC client or approved equivalent - **Local dev:** MinIO container for object storage; Redis Streams or RQ for queue; dotenv for secrets - **Profile resolver:** `infra.adapters.resolver.get_storage_adapter()`, `get_queue_adapter()`, `get_event_adapter()`, `get_secrets_adapter()` — each reads `DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE` env var - **Configuration:** Pydantic Settings v2 model per adapter; validated at import time; fails fast on missing required vars - **Health check:** each adapter exposes a `health_check() -> bool` method; callable from a `/health/adapters` FastAPI route - **Test expectations:** unit tests with mocked boto3 and mock queue client for both profiles; integration test with MinIO and Redis for local profile; no live AWS calls in CI - **Documentation:** `docs/infra/adapters.md` describing each adapter interface, env vars, and profile selection - **Gate:** both aws and onprem adapter unit tests must pass; Pydantic config validation must fail fast on missing vars; no hardcoded credentials - **Forbidden:** hardcoded AWS region, bucket names, or queue URLs in application code; direct boto3 calls outside adapter layer ### Acceptance — REQ-002 - `DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE=aws` resolves S3Adapter, SQSAdapter, SNSAdapter, SecretsManagerAdapter without error - `DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE=onprem` resolves S3CompatibleAdapter, ApprovedQueueAdapter, ApprovedEventAdapter, VaultAdapter without error - `DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE=local` resolves MinIO-backed and Redis-backed adapters for local development - All adapter interfaces define typed abstract methods; concrete implementations satisfy the interface contract verified by isinstance checks in tests - Pydantic Settings validation raises a clear startup error when a required env var is missing for the selected profile - Unit tests for both aws and onprem profiles pass without live infrastructure using mocked clients - Integration test with MinIO container confirms object upload, download, and delete via ObjectStorageAdapter - `health_check()` returns True for all adapters when backing services are reachable - No hardcoded credentials, bucket names, or queue URLs appear in source; all resolved via config - `docs/infra/adapters.md` documents all adapter interfaces, env vars, and profile selection logic ### Out of Scope — REQ-002 - Observability sink adapters (REQ-014) - AI/GPU runtime adapters (REQ-012) - Secrets rotation automation - Multi-region failover logic - CDN or edge delivery adapters ### Future Compatibility — REQ-002 - All application REQs (REQ-003 through REQ-013) must import adapters exclusively from `src/infra/adapters` - Adapter interface method signatures are stable contracts; new methods may be added but existing signatures must not change - Profile resolver factory functions are the canonical entry points; application code must not instantiate adapter classes directly - Local dev mode must remain available for all adapter types to support developer onboarding and CI without live infra --- ### Functional Scope — REQ-003 This REQ delivers the document ingest API and the object storage pipeline. It is the entry point for all documents entering the Zen 2030 platform and the first step in the document lifecycle: a document is uploaded, stored in profile-resolved object storage, and an IngestRecord is created with state Pending. An ingest event is published to the profile-resolved queue to trigger downstream OCR/IDP processing. This REQ belongs to the broader scenario of the full document lifecycle from upload to validated archive. It delivers the ingest slice only; OCR, classification, and validation are deferred to REQ-004 and REQ-005. **Delivered now:** - REST API endpoint: `POST /api/v1/documents/ingest` — accepts multipart file upload (pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx, jpg, png) - File validation: MIME type check, max file size enforcement, filename sanitization - Object storage upload via ObjectStorageAdapter (profile-resolved) - IngestRecord creation in DB with state=Pending, ingest_ref (UUID), original_filename, mime_type, storage_key, uploaded_by - Document record creation linked to IngestRecord - Ingest event published to queue: `{ event: "document.ingested", document_id, ingest_ref, storage_key, mime_type }` - API response: `{ document_id, ingest_ref, state: "Pending", storage_key }` - Auth: endpoint requires authenticated user (JWT/session); uploaded_by populated from token claims - Audit log entry created for ingest action **Intentionally deferred:** - OCR and classification (REQ-004) - Validation workflow (REQ-005) - Batch ingest or bulk upload - Webhook callbacks on ingest completion **Future REQs may safely assume:** - IngestRecord with state=Pending and a valid storage_key exists before OCR pipeline starts - `document.ingested` event schema is stable: document_id, ingest_ref, storage_key, mime_type - storage_key format is `{profile}/{year}/{month}/{document_id}/{filename}` ### Technical Scope — REQ-003 - **Lane:** python (backend, FastAPI) - **Runtime profile:** aws, on-prem, local (all three via adapter) - **Primary module:** `src/api/ingest/` (FastAPI router) + `src/core/ingest/` (ingest service, file validator) - **API:** `POST /api/v1/documents/ingest` — multipart/form-data; returns 201 with IngestRecord summary - **File validation:** python-magic for MIME detection; configurable max_file_size_mb; filename sanitization via pathlib - **Object storage:** ObjectStorageAdapter.upload(key, file_bytes, content_type) — key format: `{profile}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{document_id}/{sanitized_filename}` - **DB:** SQLAlchemy async session; creates Document + IngestRecord atomically in one transaction - **Queue:** QueueAdapter.publish(queue_name, message_dict) — message: `{ event, document_id, ingest_ref, storage_key, mime_type, timestamp }` - **Auth:** FastAPI dependency `get_current_user` returning User from JWT claims; uploaded_by = user.id - **Audit:** AuditLog entry: action=INGEST, entity_type=Document, entity_id=document_id, actor=user.id - **Error handling:** 400 for unsupported MIME, 413 for oversized file, 422 for validation errors, 500 with structured error body - **Test expectations:** happy path upload test with MinIO mock; MIME rejection test; oversized file test; DB state assertion; queue message assertion; auth deny test (401) - **Documentation:** OpenAPI schema auto-generated; curl example in `runs/kit/REQ-003/test/api/ingest.http` - **Gate:** 80% coverage on `src/api/ingest/` and `src/core/ingest/`; no secrets in source ### Acceptance — REQ-003 - `POST /api/v1/documents/ingest` with a valid PDF returns 201 with document_id, ingest_ref, state=Pending, storage_key - IngestRecord and Document records exist in DB with correct fields after successful upload - File is present in profile-resolved object storage at the expected storage_key path - Queue message `{ event: "document.ingested", document_id, ingest_ref, storage_key, mime_type }` is published after successful ingest - AuditLog entry with action=INGEST is created for the document - Upload of an unsupported MIME type returns 400 with a descriptive error body - Upload exceeding max file size returns 413 - Unauthenticated request returns 401 - Unit tests pass for both aws and onprem adapter profiles using mocked clients - OpenAPI schema documents the ingest endpoint; curl example file exists at `runs/kit/REQ-003/test/api/ingest.http` ### Out of Scope — REQ-003 - OCR, parsing, or classification (REQ-004) - Validation workflow (REQ-005) - Batch or bulk ingest - Webhook or callback on ingest completion - Document deduplication logic ### Future Compatibility — REQ-003 - IngestRecord state=Pending and storage_key are stable preconditions for REQ-004 OCR pipeline - `document.ingested` event schema (document_id, ingest_ref, storage_key, mime_type) is stable for REQ-004 queue consumer - storage_key format is stable for all downstream REQs that retrieve document bytes from object storage - `get_current_user` FastAPI dependency is stable for all subsequent API REQs --- ### Functional Scope — REQ-004 This REQ delivers the OCR, IDP (Intelligent Document Processing), and classification pipeline. It consumes the `document.ingested` event from the queue, retrieves the document from object storage, runs OCR and parsing, classifies the document, and transitions the document state to AwaitingValidation. This REQ belongs to the broader scenario of automated document processing before human validation. It delivers the automated processing slice; human validation is deferred to REQ-005. **Delivered now:** - Queue consumer worker: listens for `document.ingested` events on the profile-resolved queue - Document retrieval from object storage via ObjectStorageAdapter - OCR pipeline: Tesseract for image-based PDFs and images; PaddleOCR/docTR as configurable alternative - Parsing pipeline: Apache Tika for docx/xlsx/pptx; Unstructured for mixed-format extraction - Text extraction result stored as DocumentVersion with extracted_text, page_count, extraction_method - Classification: configurable rules engine (keyword/regex rules per category); optional layout-aware model hook (interface only, model loading deferred) - Classification result stored on Document: classification_category, confidence_score, classification_method - Document state transition: Processing → AwaitingValidation (atomic DB update) - Event published: `{ event: "document.awaiting_validation", document_id, classification_category, confidence_score }` - Audit log entry: action=OCR_COMPLETE + action=CLASSIFIED **Intentionally deferred:** - Human validation (REQ-005) - Layout-aware model loading and inference (configurable hook present, model loading deferred) - Re-processing on validation rejection (REQ-007) **Future REQs may safely assume:** - Document in AwaitingValidation state has extracted_text in DocumentVersion and classification_category + confidence_score on Document - `document.awaiting_validation` event schema is stable ### Technical Scope — REQ-004 - **Lane:** python (backend, worker process) - **Runtime profile:** aws, on-prem, local (queue consumer runs in all profiles) - **Primary module:** `src/core/ocr/` (OCR + parsing) + `src/core/classification/` (rules engine) + `src/workers/ingest_worker.py` (queue consumer) - **Queue consumer:** async worker using QueueAdapter.consume(); handles message ack/nack; retry on transient failure (max 3 retries with backoff) - **OCR:** pytesseract wrapper + PaddleOCR/docTR as configurable backend (env var `OCR_BACKEND=tesseract|paddleocr|doctr`) - **Parsing:** tika-python for docx/xlsx/pptx; unstructured for mixed formats; dispatch by MIME type - **Classification:** `ClassificationEngine` with pluggable rule sets loaded from YAML config; returns category + confidence float; optional model hook interface defined but not loaded - **DB:** atomic update of Document (state, classification_category, confidence_score) + insert DocumentVersion (extracted_text, page_count, extraction_method) in one transaction - **Event publish:** QueueAdapter or EventAdapter publish `document.awaiting_validation` - **Error handling:** on OCR failure, document transitions to state=Rejected with error_reason; audit log entry; dead-letter queue message published - **Test expectations:** unit tests for OCR dispatch by MIME; classification rules engine with sample fixtures; state transition test (Processing → AwaitingValidation); failure path test (OCR error → Rejected) - **Gate:** 80% coverage on `src/core/ocr/`, `src/core/classification/`, `src/workers/` ### Acceptance — REQ-004 - Worker consumes `document.ingested` event and retrieves document bytes from object storage - PDF document produces a DocumentVersion record with non-empty extracted_text and correct page_count - DOCX document is parsed via Tika and produces a DocumentVersion record with extracted_text - Classification engine assigns classification_category and confidence_score to Document after processing - Document state transitions from Processing to AwaitingValidation atomically after successful OCR and classification - `document.awaiting_validation` event is published with document_id, classification_category, confidence_score - AuditLog entries for OCR_COMPLETE and CLASSIFIED actions are created - On OCR failure, document transitions to Rejected state and a dead-letter queue message is published - Unit tests cover OCR dispatch by MIME type, classification rules, state transition, and failure path - OCR backend is selectable via `OCR_BACKEND` env var without code changes ### Out of Scope — REQ-004 - Human validation (REQ-005) - Layout-aware model inference beyond the hook interface - Re-processing triggered by validator rejection (REQ-007) - Multi-page document splitting or merging ### Future Compatibility — REQ-004 - AwaitingValidation state with extracted_text and classification fields is the stable precondition for REQ-005 - `document.awaiting_validation` event schema is stable for REQ-005 and REQ-007 - ClassificationEngine interface is stable for REQ-007 re-routing logic - OCR backend env var pattern is stable for operational configuration --- ### Functional Scope — REQ-005 This REQ delivers the human validation API and the document lifecycle state machine enforcement. It is the critical control point that ensures no document reaches Validated state without explicit human approval. Validators can approve or reject documents in AwaitingValidation state via a REST API. Rejection returns the document to a reviewable state with a rejection reason. This REQ belongs to the broader scenario of mandatory human-in-the-loop validation before any downstream use (archive search, export, AI RAG). It delivers the validation API and state machine; the operator UI is deferred to REQ-006. **Delivered now:** - REST API: `GET /api/v1/documents/validation-queue` — lists documents in AwaitingValidation state (paginated, filterable by category) - REST API: `GET /api/v1/documents/{document_id}/validation` — returns document detail with extracted_text, classification, and validation history - REST API: `POST /api/v1/documents/{document_id}/validate` — body: `{ action: "approve"|"reject", reason?: string }` - State machine enforcement: only AwaitingValidation → Validated (approve) or AwaitingValidation → Rejected (reject) transitions are permitted - ValidationRecord created: validator_id, action, reason, validated_at - AuditLog entry: action=VALIDATED or action=REJECTED - Event published: `{ event: "document.validated"|"document.rejected", document_id, validator_id, action }` - RBAC: only users with role=validator or role=admin may call the validate endpoint - Unauthorized access returns 403 with audit log entry **Intentionally deferred:** - Operator UI (REQ-006) - Workflow routing on rejection (REQ-007) - Bulk validation actions **Future REQs may safely assume:** - Validated state is only reachable via this API with a human actor - ValidationRecord with validator_id and validated_at is present for every Validated document - `document.validated` event schema is stable: document_id, validator_id, action, timestamp ### Technical Scope — REQ-005 - **Lane:** python (backend, FastAPI) - **Runtime profile:** aws, on-prem, local - **Primary module:** `src/api/validation/` (FastAPI router) + `src/core/validation/` (state machine, validation service) - **State machine:** `DocumentStateMachine` class enforcing allowed transitions; raises `InvalidTransitionError` on illegal state change - **RBAC:** FastAPI dependency `require_role(["validator", "admin"])` applied to validate endpoint; returns 403 on failure - **DB:** atomic update of Document.state + insert ValidationRecord in one transaction; optimistic locking via version field on Document - **Event publish:** EventAdapter.publish(`document.validated` or `document.rejected`) - **Audit:** AuditLog entry per validation action with actor, action, entity_id, timestamp - **Pagination:** validation queue uses cursor-based pagination; default page_size=20 - **Error handling:** 409 on invalid state transition; 403 on RBAC failure with audit log; 404 on unknown document_id - **Test expectations:** approve happy path; reject happy path; invalid transition test (Pending → Validated must fail); RBAC deny test (viewer role returns 403); audit log assertion; event publish assertion - **Gate:** 80% coverage on `src/api/validation/` and `src/core/validation/` ### Acceptance — REQ-005 - `POST /api/v1/documents/{document_id}/validate` with action=approve transitions document to Validated state and creates ValidationRecord - `POST /api/v1/documents/{document_id}/validate` with action=reject transitions document to Rejected state with reason stored - Attempting to validate a document not in AwaitingValidation state returns 409 with descriptive error - Only users with role=validator or role=admin can call the validate endpoint; viewer role returns 403 - 403 response is accompanied by an AuditLog entry recording the unauthorized attempt - ValidationRecord contains validator_id, action, reason (if reject), and validated_at timestamp - AuditLog entries for VALIDATED and REJECTED actions are created with correct actor and entity references - `document.validated` or `document.rejected` event is published after each validation action - `GET /api/v1/documents/validation-queue` returns only AwaitingValidation documents with correct pagination - Unit tests cover approve, reject, invalid transition, RBAC deny, audit log, and event publish paths ### Out of Scope — REQ-005 - Operator validation UI (REQ-006) - Workflow routing on rejection (REQ-007) - Bulk validation or batch approval - Automated validation bypass of any kind ### Future Compatibility — REQ-005 - Validated state reachable only via this API is a hard invariant for REQ-008 (archive), REQ-010 (export), and REQ-012 (AI RAG) - ValidationRecord schema (validator_id, action, reason, validated_at) is stable for REQ-007 and REQ-008 - `document.validated` event schema is stable for REQ-007 workflow routing and REQ-012 embedding trigger - `DocumentStateMachine` is the canonical state transition authority; no other code may mutate Document.state directly --- ### Functional Scope — REQ-006 This REQ delivers the validation workflow operator UI.
